original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Searching below C=40 in the #2017 Eisenstein binary scalar-rectangle or fixed-support block-linear additive pairing model; specify a changed premise instead. This bound does not cover every complex decoder.

actual_scope: For every 25-line puncture of the 120 E8 root lines, classify root-normal supports with live label span at most seven, derive the separate COPY floor for exact eight-term root-pair dual-basis decoders, and price the best compatible profile under the pinned selected-word ceiling.
scope_change_reason: The selector card focuses on larger-rank block climbs. The bounded experiment changes the proved eight-term all-pairs puncture range from p<=24 to exactly p=25 and restricts the decoder to root-pair dual bases. This is the first support-rank boundary beyond the prior floor and gives a precise exact mask census; the selected-word screen rejects this family before network synthesis.
bottleneck_link: A support-rank drop can lower the copied-information charge and replace rank-eight centre children with smaller-rank children. The complete favorable profile test determines whether this newly reachable boundary can change the selected recursive moment.
stop_rule: Enumerate all 130305 distinct functional pairs for each of 120 root normals, classify every size-25 extremal mask, prove the root-pair copy floor, and screen its best compatible histogram. Stop without searching another family if its zero-overhead ceiling is below the selected word.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json: 7560 distinct p=25 masks, each shared by one root normal only; every residual support has dimension seven; root-pair COPY >=54; exact best-case a upper 0.001538546310036, below selected 0.001690054109089 and the +5% gate.
author: Cinna Davis
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in scope selection, exact enumeration, proof development, cost screening, verifier implementation, and writing. No independent human or proof-assistant review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can a non-root dual basis or an overcomplete/masked decoder at p=25 avoid the one-exceptional-root restriction and pass the fully charged local moment gate?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The exact result closes only eight-term root-pair dual bases; a broader support alphabet may permit several larger-rank children and change the paid local profile.
open_questions.first_step: Choose one explicit non-root support alphabet, derive its exact F2 support-rank floor, and screen the complete per-call profile before constructing a network.
open_questions.blocked_by: No source-aligned frame or complete setup, hosting, precision, and restoration invoice is currently identified for a changed support alphabet.
